channel.title: Thoughts by Your Hommie
channel.description: Statistical and machine learning cases, simulations that verify beliefs before the data arrives, and stats textbooks rewritten simpler.

item.title: The IQ gap between men and women, simulated
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: A group difference of a few points is usually argued with anecdotes. Simulated, it becomes arithmetic: how far the two distributions overlap, what share of the extremes each group supplies, and how often a randomly chosen pair reverses the group verdict.

item.title: Which Nigerian states got worse, and their deadliest months
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Work in progress — a hierarchical negative-binomial model over Nigeria’s 772 state-LGA cells, fitted on 2015–2025 and scored out of sample on 2026, with gradient boosting kept as a scored control rather than a rival for the headline.

item.title: How big should the spoon be?
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: A correctly drawn five hundred beats a biased forty thousand. In a simulated country where the true result is fixed before anyone is interviewed, 500 interviews drawn from the whole register name the winner in 99.2% of runs and 40,000 drawn only from phone owners name it in none of them. Nasir El-Rufai dismissed Nigeria’s 2023 polls for the wrong reason, and had the right one in his next sentence.

item.title: The standard error, rewritten without the sampling-distribution detour
item.dc:creator: Batesthommie
item.description: Most textbooks introduce the standard error by first constructing an imaginary population of repeated samples. That detour is where readers lose the thread, and it is avoidable.
